prompt: An object is released from rest and falls through air until it reaches terminal velocity. State what the gradient of its velocity-time graph represents, and describe how this gradient changes from release until terminal velocity is reached.
hints: Recall the physical meaning of the gradient of a velocity-time graph.
How does acceleration change as air resistance builds up?
solution: The gradient of the velocity-time graph represents acceleration. The gradient starts at 9.81 m s^-2 at t = 0 and decreases continuously until it becomes zero at terminal velocity.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: State that gradient of v-t graph equals acceleration.
Step 2: Describe the initial gradient as 9.81 m s^-2 (or g).
Step 3: Describe that gradient decreases continuously to zero as speed approaches terminal velocity.

mark_scheme.criterion: Gradient decreases continuously from 9.81 m s^-2 (at t = 0) to zero (at terminal velocity)
